label: lem:identities
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The partitions with largest part $n$ have generating function $q^n/(q;q)_n$. Since $(q;q)_\infty/(q;q)_n=(q^{n+1};q)_\infty$, this gives the first and third expressions. A partition into distinct parts with smallest part $n$ consists of the part $n$ together with a set of distinct parts exceeding $n$, so
\[
\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{D},\ \operatorname{sm}(\lambda)=n}(-1)^{\ell(\lambda)}q^{|\lambda|}=-q^n\prod_{m>n}(1-q^m),
\]
which gives the second. All series converge absolutely because $f$ is bounded. For~\eqref{eq:mass}, put $P_n=(q^{n+1};q)_\infty$; then $P_n-P_{n-1}=q^nP_n=\omega_n(q)$, so $\sum_{n=1}^N\omega_n(q)=P_N-(q;q)_\infty$, and $P_N\to1$.
head: environment

label: thm:wiener
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:wiener}
Let $\Phi\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ and $K\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ with $\widehat K(\xi)=\int_\mathbb{R} K(z)e^{-i\xi z}\,\mathrm{d} z\ne0$ for all $\xi\in\mathbb{R}$. If $(K*\Phi)(w)\to a\widehat K(0)$ as $|w|\to\infty$, then $(k*\Phi)(w)\to a\widehat k(0)$ as $|w|\to\infty$ for every $k\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$.
head: environment
name: Wiener

label: lem:abelstep
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:abelstep}
Let $\Theta\in L^\infty([0,\infty))$ satisfy $\int_w^{w+c}\Theta\to0$ as $w\to\infty$ for every $c>0$. Then $\int_0^\infty\Theta(v)k(v-w)\,\mathrm{d} v\to0$ as $w\to\infty$ for every $k\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For $k=\mathbf 1_{[a,b]}$ and $w>-a$ the integral equals $\int_{w+a}^{w+b}\Theta\to0$. By linearity the claim holds for step functions. For general $k$ and a step function $k_0$, the two integrals differ by at most $\|\Theta\|_\infty\|k-k_0\|_{L^1}$, and step functions are dense in $L^1(\mathbb{R})$.
head: environment

label: lem:scheffe
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:scheffe}
Let $h_j\ge0$ and $h\ge 0$ be integrable on $\mathbb{R}$ with $h_j\to h$ pointwise and $\int h_j\to\int h$. Then $\int|h_j-h|\to0$.
head: environment
name: Scheff\'e

title: Proof
body_md: $\int|h_j-h|=2\int(h-h_j)^++\int h_j-\int h$, and $\int(h-h_j)^+\to0$ by dominated convergence, since $0\le(h-h_j)^+\le h$.
head: environment

label: lem:poch
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:poch}
Fix $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, write $q=q_t(\beta)$, and for $|a|\le1$ put $\log(aq;q)_\infty=\sum_{k\ge1}\mathrm{Log}(1-aq^k)$ with the principal branch.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] Uniformly for $|a|\le1$ and $0<t\le1$, $\log(aq;q)_\infty=-\mathrm{Li}_2(a)/\tau+O_\beta(\log(2/t))$.
\item[(b)] For fixed $a$ with $|a|=1$, $a\ne1$, as $t\to0^+$,
\[
\frac{(q;q)_\infty}{(aq;q)_\infty}=\Big(\frac{2\pi}{\tau}\Big)^{1/2}(1-a)^{1/2}\exp\Big(-\frac{\pi^2/6-\mathrm{Li}_2(a)}{\tau}\Big)\,(1+o(1)),
\]
with principal square roots. In particular, for $a=e^{i\vartheta}$, $0<\vartheta<2\pi$,
\[
\Big|\frac{(q;q)_\infty}{(e^{i\vartheta}q;q)_\infty}\Big|=\frac{(2\pi|1-e^{i\vartheta}|)^{1/2}}{(1+\beta^2)^{1/4}\,t^{1/2}}\,\exp\Big(\frac{\kappa_\beta(\vartheta)}{t}\Big)(1+o(1)).
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $L\in\mathbb{C}$. A bounded function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfies condition $(\mathrm{SI}_L)$ if for every fixed $c>0$,
\[
\sum_{x<n\le x+cx/\log x}f(n)=\frac{cLx}{\log x}+o\Big(\frac{x}{\log x}\Big)\qquad(x\to\infty).
\]
A set $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ satisfies $(\mathrm{SI}_L)$ if $\mathbf 1_S$ does.
head: environment

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: thm:abelian
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:abelian}
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$ be bounded, $d\in\mathbb{C}$, $E(x)=\sum_{n\le x}f(n)-dx$, and suppose
\[
\varepsilon:=\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{|E(x)|\log x}{x}<\infty .
\]
Then $\displaystyle\limsup_{q\to1^-}|\mathcal{A}_f(q)-d|\le\frac{2\varepsilon}{e}$.
head: environment

label: cor:consequences
title: Corollary
head: environment

label: thm:counter
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: cor:ND
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:ND}
There is a set $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ of natural density $\tfrac12$ such that $\liminf_{q\to1^-}F_S(q)=0$ and $\limsup_{q\to1^-}F_S(q)=1$. Consequently, the existence of $M(f)$ does not imply convergence of $\mathcal{A}_f(q)$ as $q\to 1^-$, even for indicator functions and radial approach, and the formula~\eqref{eq:OSWlimit} does not hold for all sets possessing a natural density.
head: environment

label: rem:onec
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:onec}
In condition $(\mathrm{SI}_L)$ the quantifier ``for every $c>0$'' cannot be replaced by a single value of $c$. Given $c_0>0$, apply Theorem~\ref{thm:counter}(a) with $\theta=2\pi/c_0$. By~\eqref{eq:window-osc} below, $A_S(x+c_0x/\log x)-A_S(x)=c_0x/(2\log x)+o(x/\log x)$, yet $F_S(q)$ oscillates with amplitude $\delta(2\pi^2/(c_0\sinh(2\pi^2/c_0)))^{1/2}>0$. The obstruction is that the Fourier transform of $\mathbf 1_{[0,c_0]}$ vanishes at $\xi=2\pi/c_0=\theta$, so a single window length cannot detect oscillation of $\Phi_{\mathbf 1_S}$ at that frequency.
head: environment

label: ex:examples
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:examples}
(1) If $S$ is a union of $s$ residue classes modulo $m$, then $A_S(x)=sx/m+O(1)$. For $k\ge2$ let $Q_k$ be the set of $k$-free integers; then $A_{Q_k}(x)=\sum_{d\le x^{1/k}}\mu(d)\lfloor x/d^k\rfloor=x/\zeta(k)+O(x^{1/k})$. Corollary~\ref{cor:consequences}(a) gives $F_S(q)\to s/m$ and $F_{Q_k}(q)\to1/\zeta(k)$, recovering the corresponding radial formulas of~\cite{OSW1,OSW2}.

(2) The prime number theorem with the classical error term gives, for some $c_1>0$, the bound $\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\ll x\exp(-c_1\sqrt{\log x})$ (see~\cite[Chapter~6]{MV}). Hence $\mathcal{A}_\mu(q)\to0$, that is,
\[
\lim_{q\to1^-}\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{D}\setminus\{\emptyset\}}\mu_{\mathcal{P}}(\lambda)\,\mu(\operatorname{sm}(\lambda))\,q^{|\lambda|}=0 .
\]

(3) Let $\mathbb P$ be the set of primes. Here $A_{\mathbb P}(x)\sim x/\log x$, so Theorem~\ref{thm:abelian} gives only $\limsup F_{\mathbb P}(q)\le 2/e$. However, $\pi(x)=x/\log x+o(x/\log x)$ gives $\pi(x+cx/\log x)-\pi(x)=o(x/\log x)$, so $(\mathrm{SI}_0)$ holds and Theorem~\ref{thm:main} gives $F_{\mathbb P}(q)\to0$. Thus condition $(\mathrm{SI}_L)$ is strictly weaker than the hypothesis of Corollary~\ref{cor:consequences}(a).
head: environment

label: thm:primes
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: cor:primesuff
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:primesuff}
Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, $\alpha\ge0$, $\delta\ge0$, and $\mathrm{li}_\alpha(x)=\int_2^x(\log y)^{-\alpha}\,\mathrm{d} y$, so that $\mathrm{li}_1=\mathrm{li}$. If $A_S(x)=\delta\,\mathrm{li}_\alpha(x)+\delta'x/(\log x)^{1+\alpha}+o(x/(\log x)^{1+\alpha})$ for some $\delta'\in\mathbb{R}$, then $(\log(1/(1-q)))^{\alpha}F_S(q)\to\delta$ as $q\to1^-$.
head: environment

label: cor:chebotarev
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:chebotarev}
Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be a finite Galois extension, let $C\subseteq\mathrm{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)$ be a conjugacy class, and let $\mathbb P_C$ be the set of primes $p$ unramified in $K$ whose Frobenius class is $C$. Then
\[
\lim_{q\to1^-}\log\frac1{1-q}\cdot\Big(-\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\mathcal{D}\setminus\{\emptyset\}\\ \operatorname{sm}(\lambda)\in\mathbb P_C}}\mu_{\mathcal{P}}(\lambda)q^{|\lambda|}\Big)=\frac{|C|}{[K:\mathbb Q]}.
\]
In particular, for coprime integers $\ell$ and $k\ge1$,
\[
\lim_{q\to1^-}\log\frac1{1-q}\cdot\Big(-\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\mathcal{D}\setminus\{\emptyset\},\ \operatorname{sm}(\lambda)\ \mathrm{prime}\\ \operatorname{sm}(\lambda)\equiv\ell\ (\mathrm{mod}\ k)}}\mu_{\mathcal{P}}(\lambda)q^{|\lambda|}\Big)=\frac1{\varphi(k)} .
\]
head: environment

label: thm:periodic
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: cor:AP
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:AP}
For $m\ge3$ let
\[
\beta_m=\min_{1\le j<m/2}\frac{\gamma(2\pi j/m)}{\mathrm{Cl}_2(2\pi j/m)} .
\]
Let $r\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $S_{r,m}=\{n\ge1:\ n\equiv r\ (\mathrm{mod}\ m)\}$. If $|\beta|<\beta_m$, then $F_{S_{r,m}}(q_t)\to1/m$; if $|\beta|\ge\beta_m$, then $F_{S_{r,m}}(q_t)$ is unbounded as $t\to0^+$. For $m\le2$, $F_{S_{r,m}}(q_t)\to1/m$ for every $\beta$. Moreover
\[
\beta_m\le\frac{\pi}{2\,(1+\log(m/2\pi))}\longrightarrow0\qquad(m\to\infty),
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\beta_3&=\frac{2\pi^2}{9\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(2\pi/3)}=3.24143587\ldots,\qquad \beta_4=\frac{3\pi^2}{16\,G}=2.02032787\ldots,\\
\beta_6&=\frac{5\pi^2}{36\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3)}=1.35059828\ldots,
\end{aligned}
\]
where $G$ is Catalan's constant.
head: environment

label: thm:instability
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:instability}
For $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ put
\[
\Lambda_\beta(s)=-\mathrm{Re}\,\frac{\mathrm{Li}_2\big(e^{-s(1+i\beta)}\big)}{1+i\beta}\quad(s\ge0),\qquad \Psi_\beta=\sup_{s>0}\Lambda_\beta(s),
\]
Let $\beta\ne0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\Psi_\beta\ge(e^{-s_\beta}-e^{-2s_\beta})(1+\beta^2)^{-1/2}>0$ with $s_\beta=(\pi-\arctan|\beta|)/|\beta|$, and
\[
\max_{n\ge1}|\omega_n(q_t)|=\exp\Big(\frac{\Psi_\beta}{t}+O_\beta\big(\log(2/t)\big)\Big)\qquad(0<t\le1).
\]
\item[(b)] For each $k\ge1$ choose, independently and with probability $\frac12$ each, one element of $\{2k-1,2k\}$, and let $S$ be the resulting random set. Then every outcome satisfies $|A_S(x)-x/2|\le1$ for all $x$, and hence $F_S(q)\to\frac12$ as $q\to1^-$. Almost surely, $\limsup_{t\to0^+}|F_S(q_t(\beta))|=\infty$ simultaneously for all $\beta$ in any prescribed countable subset of $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: cor:stolz
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:stolz}
In every Stolz sector at $1$ with $M_0>1$ there are paths along which $F_S(q)$ is unbounded for some arithmetic progression $S$, and for almost every random set $S$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:instability}(b). In particular, the Stolz-sector statements~\cite[Theorem~1.1 and Corollaries~1.2 and~1.3]{Schneider} fail already for periodic functions and for sets of bounded discrepancy, and the limits in~\cite[Lemma~2.5 and Theorem~1.3]{OSW1}, for $q\to1$, do not hold for unrestricted approach from within the unit disk.
head: environment

label: lem:gumbel
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gumbel}
For $0<t\le1$ and $q=e^{-t}$,
\[
\sum_{n\ge1}\Big|\omega_n(q)-t\,g\big(nt-L_t\big)\Big|\le 8t .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $n\ge1$ and put $y=e^{-nt}\in(0,1)$. Since $te^{L_t}=1$,
\[
t\,g(nt-L_t)=t\,e^{-nt+L_t}\exp\!\big(-e^{-nt+L_t}\big)=y\,e^{-h},\qquad h:=\frac yt,
\]
while $\omega_n(q)=y\,e^{-H}$ with
\[
H:=-\log(q^{n+1};q)_\infty=\sum_{m>n}\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{q^{km}}{k}=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k\,\frac{e^{-knt}}{e^{kt}-1}.
\]
The term $k=1$ equals $y/(e^t-1)$, and $0<\frac1t-\frac1{e^t-1}<\frac12$ for $t>0$. For $k\ge2$ we use $e^{kt}-1\ge kt$. Hence
\[
-\frac y2\le H-h\le\frac1t\sum_{k\ge2}\frac{y^k}{k^2}\le\frac{y^2}{t}.
\]
In particular $\min(H,h)\ge h-\frac12$. By the mean value theorem, $|e^{-H}-e^{-h}|\le e^{-\min(H,h)}|H-h|$, and therefore
\[
\big|\omega_n(q)-t\,g(nt-L_t)\big|\le e^{1/2}\,y\,e^{-y/t}\Big(\frac y2+\frac{y^2}t\Big)=e^{1/2}\,t^2\,p(s_n),
\]
where $s_n=e^{-nt}/t$ and $p(s)=s^2(\frac12+s)e^{-s}$. The logarithmic derivative $2/s+1/(\frac12+s)-1$ of $p$ is strictly decreasing, so $p$ is unimodal on $(0,\infty)$, and $\max p\le2$. As $x\mapsto s(x)=e^{-xt}/t$ is decreasing, $Q(x):=t^2p(s(x))$ is unimodal on $[0,\infty)$. For a nonnegative unimodal function, $\sum_{n\ge1}Q(n)\le\int_0^\infty Q+\max Q$. The substitution $s=s(x)$, $\,\mathrm{d} x=-\,\mathrm{d} s/(ts)$, gives
\[
\int_0^\infty Q(x)\,\mathrm{d} x=t\int_0^{1/t}\frac{p(s)}{s}\,\mathrm{d} s\le t\int_0^\infty s\Big(\frac12+s\Big)e^{-s}\,\mathrm{d} s=\frac{5t}{2}.
\]
Hence the sum in the lemma is at most $e^{1/2}(\frac52t+2t^2)\le\frac92e^{1/2}t<8t$. The constant $8$ is not optimal; the arguments below use only the order $O(t)$.
head: environment

label: lem:reduction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:reduction}
There is a function $\eta:(0,1/e)\to[0,\infty)$ with $\eta(t)\to0$ as $t\to0^+$ such that, for every bounded $f$ and every $t\in(0,1/e)$,
\[
\big|\mathcal{A}_f(e^{-t})-J_f(w(t))\big|\le\eta(t)\,\lVert f\rVert_\infty .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $k_t(x)=t\,g(tx-L_t)$. We compare $\mathcal{A}_f(e^{-t})=\sum f(n)\omega_n$ with $J_f(w(t))$ in four steps.

\emph{Step 1.} By Lemma~\ref{lem:gumbel}, $|\mathcal{A}_f(e^{-t})-\sum_{n\ge1}f(n)k_t(n)|\le8t\lVert f\rVert_\infty$.

\emph{Step 2.} Since $\psi_f=f(n)$ on $(n-1,n]$,
\[
\Big|\sum_{n\ge1}f(n)k_t(n)-\int_0^\infty\psi_f(x)k_t(x)\,\mathrm{d} x\Big|\le\lVert f\rVert_\infty\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{n-1}^n|k_t(n)-k_t(x)|\,\mathrm{d} x\le\lVert f\rVert_\infty\int_0^\infty|k_t'(y)|\,\mathrm{d} y,
\]
because $|k_t(n)-k_t(x)|\le\int_{n-1}^n|k_t'|$ for $x\in(n-1,n]$. By~\eqref{eq:gprime}, $\int_0^\infty|k_t'|\le t\int_\mathbb{R}|g'|=2t/e$.

\emph{Step 3.} $\int_0^1|\psi_f|k_t\le t\,g(0)\lVert f\rVert_\infty=t\lVert f\rVert_\infty/e$.

\emph{Step 4.} By~\eqref{eq:Jx},
\[
\Big|\int_1^\infty\psi_f(x)k_t(x)\,\mathrm{d} x-J_f(w(t))\Big|\le\lVert f\rVert_\infty\,D(t),
\]
where
\[
D(t):=\int_1^\infty\Big|t\,g(tx-L_t)-v'(x)\,g\big(v(x)-w(t)\big)\Big|\,\mathrm{d} x .
\]
Substitute $x=z_u:=(u+L_t)/t$, so that $x\ge1$ corresponds to $u\ge t-L_t$, $z_0=x_t$ and $\log z_u=L_t+\log(u+L_t)$. Put
\[
\sigma_t(u):=v(z_u)-w(t),\qquad \sigma_t'(u)=\frac{v'(z_u)}{t}=\frac{L_t+\log(u+L_t)}{u+L_t}\qquad(u\ge t-L_t).
\]
Then $t\,g(tx-L_t)\,\mathrm{d} x=g(u)\,\mathrm{d} u$ and $v'(x)g(v(x)-w(t))\,\mathrm{d} x=h_t(u)\,\mathrm{d} u$ with $h_t(u):=g(\sigma_t(u))\sigma_t'(u)$ for $u\ge t-L_t$ and $h_t(u):=0$ otherwise. Thus
\[
D(t)\le\int_\mathbb{R}|h_t(u)-g(u)|\,\mathrm{d} u .
\]
Here $h_t\ge0$ because $\log z_u\ge0$. As $\sigma_t$ increases from $\sigma_t(t-L_t)=v(1)-w(t)=-w(t)$ to $\infty$,
\[
\int_\mathbb{R} h_t=\int_{-w(t)}^\infty g=1-\mathcal G(-w(t))\longrightarrow1=\int_\mathbb{R} g\qquad(t\to0^+).
\]
For fixed $u\in\mathbb{R}$ and $L_t\to\infty$, $\sigma_t'(u')=(L_t+\log(u'+L_t))/(u'+L_t)\to1$ uniformly for $u'$ between $0$ and $u$. Since $\sigma_t(0)=0$, it follows that $\sigma_t(u)=\int_0^u\sigma_t'\to u$, and hence $h_t(u)\to g(u)$ by continuity of $g$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:scheffe}, applied along an arbitrary sequence $t_j\to0^+$, $D(t)\to0$.

Collecting the four steps, the lemma holds with $\eta(t)=8t+2t/e+t/e+\int_\mathbb{R}|h_t-g|$.
head: environment

label: lem:window
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:window}
Let $f$ be bounded and $c>0$ fixed. As $X\to\infty$,
\[
\frac{\log X}{X}\sum_{X<n\le X+cX/\log X}f(n)=\int_{v(X)}^{v(X)+c}\Phi_f(v)\,\mathrm{d} v+o(1).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $H=cX/\log X$ and $X\ge e$. First, $\sum_{X<n\le X+H}f(n)$ and $\int_X^{X+H}\psi_f$ differ by at most $2\lVert f\rVert_\infty$, since only the two unit cells $(n-1,n]$ containing $X$ or $X+H$ are cut. Second, with $x=\chi(v)$,
\[
\int_X^{X+H}\psi_f(x)\,\mathrm{d} x=\int_{v(X)}^{v(X+H)}\Phi_f(v)\chi'(v)\,\mathrm{d} v .
\]
On this range, $\chi'(v)=x/\log x$ lies between $X/\log X$ and $(X+H)/\log(X+H)\le(X/\log X)(1+c/\log X)$, because $x/\log x$ is increasing for $x\ge e$. Third, since $\log y/y$ is decreasing for $y\ge e$,
\[
c\,\frac{X\log(X+H)}{(X+H)\log X}\le v(X+H)-v(X)=\int_X^{X+H}\frac{\log y}{y}\,\mathrm{d} y\le c ,
\]
so $v(X+H)-v(X)=c+o(1)$. Combining the three observations,
\[
\frac{\log X}{X}\sum_{X<n\le X+H}f(n)=\int_{v(X)}^{v(X+H)}\Phi_f+O\Big(\frac{c^2\lVert f\rVert_\infty}{\log X}+\frac{\lVert f\rVert_\infty\log X}{X}\Big)=\int_{v(X)}^{v(X)+c}\Phi_f+o(1),
\]
where the last step uses $|\int_{v(X)+c}^{v(X+H)}\Phi_f|\le\lVert f\rVert_\infty\,|v(X+H)-v(X)-c|$.
head: environment

title: Construction
body_md:
Choose even integers $X_1<X_2<\cdots$ with $h(X_1)\ge8$ and $X_{k+1}\ge4X_k$, and put $B_k=\lfloor h(X_k)\rfloor$, so that $8\le B_k\le X_k$. Let
\[
I_k^-=(X_k,X_k+B_k]\cap\mathbb{N},\qquad I_k^+=(X_k+B_k,X_k+2B_k]\cap\mathbb{N} .
\]
These blocks lie in $(X_k,3X_k]$ and are pairwise disjoint. Define
\[
S=\Big(2\mathbb{N}\setminus\bigcup_k(I_k^-\cup I_k^+)\Big)\cup\bigcup_kI_k^+ .
\]
head: manual

title: Remark
body_md: A concrete set with the properties of Corollary~\ref{cor:ND} is $S=\{n\ge2:\ \lfloor(\log n)^{3/2}\rfloor\ \text{even}\}$. Its $j$-th block $[e^{j^{2/3}},e^{(j+1)^{2/3}})$ has length $\asymp x(\log x)^{-1/2}$ at height $x$. The block lengths increase with $j$, and the numbers of integers in consecutive blocks differ from these lengths by at most $1$. The alternating sum of these counts therefore gives $A_S(x)=x/2+O(x(\log x)^{-1/2})$, the rounding contributing only $O((\log x)^{3/2})$. On the other hand, taking $x_t$ at the midpoint of a block of length $B$ at height $x$, the block contains all $n$ with $|nt-L_t|<M$, where $M=tB/2\asymp(\log x)^{1/2}\to\infty$. The argument above then applies verbatim.
head: environment

label: lem:muwindows
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $w$ be large and $X=\chi(w)$. Then $\chi(w+c)=X\exp(\sqrt{2w+2c}-\sqrt{2w})\le X\exp(c/\log X)$. For $n\in(X,\chi(w+c+1)]$, uniformly, $(\log n)^{1+\alpha}/n=((\log X)^{1+\alpha}/X)(1+o(1))$.

(a) The interval $(X,\chi(w+1)]$ is covered by at most three intervals $(z,z+z/\log z]$ with $X\le z\le2X$. By~\eqref{eq:B} it contains $O(X/(\log X)^{1+\alpha})$ elements of $S$, each of weight at most $(\log X)^{1+\alpha}/X$. Bounded $w$ contribute a finite amount.

(b) Put $Y_c=X+cX/\log X$. By the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:window}, $v(Y_c)=w+c+o(1)$, hence
\[
\mu_S\big((w,v(Y_c)]\big)=\frac{(\log X)^{1+\alpha}}{X}\big(A_S(Y_c)-A_S(X)\big)(1+o(1)),
\]
and by~\eqref{eq:B} the factor $1+o(1)$ may be replaced by an additive $o(1)$. Let $0<\eta<c$. For large $w$ we have $w+c-\eta\le v(Y_c)\le w+c+\eta$ and $v(Y_{c-\eta})\le w+c\le v(Y_{c+\eta})$. Both the $\mu_S$-mass and the count increase with $c$, so each of the two window conditions places the other quantity between its values at $c-\eta$ and $c+\eta$, up to $o(1)$. Letting $\eta\to0$ proves the equivalence.
head: environment

label: lem:primesreduction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:primesreduction}
If $S$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:B}, then $L_t^{\alpha}F_S(e^{-t})-I_S(w(t))\to0$ as $t\to0^+$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $L=L_t\ge8$ and, for $n\in S$, put $u_n=tn-L$. As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:reduction} we have $\log n=L+\log(u_n+L)$, $v(n)-w(t)=\sigma_t(u_n)$ and $\log n/n=t\,\sigma_t'(u_n)$. Put
\[
a_n=L^{\alpha}t\,g(u_n),\qquad b_n=\frac{(\log n)^{1+\alpha}}{n}\,g\big(\sigma_t(u_n)\big)=t(\log n)^{\alpha}\sigma_t'(u_n)\,g\big(\sigma_t(u_n)\big).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:gumbel}, $|L^{\alpha}F_S(e^{-t})-\sum_{n\in S}a_n|\le8tL^{\alpha}\to0$, and $I_S(w(t))=\sum_{n\in S}b_n$.

\emph{Counting.} Let $N_j=\#\{n\in S:\ j\le u_n<j+1\}$ for integers $j\ge j_0:=\lfloor-L/2\rfloor$. These $n$ lie in $[y,y+1/t)$ with $y=(L+j)/t$, $L+j\ge L/2-1\ge3$, and $\log y=L+\log(L+j)$. Since $(L+\log(L+j))/(L+j)\le4$, this interval is covered by at most five intervals $(z,z+z/\log z]$ with $y-1\le z\le2(y+1/t)$. By~\eqref{eq:B}, and since $\log(L+j)\ge0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Nj}
N_j\le\frac{10C(L+j+1)}{t\,(L+\log(L+j))^{1+\alpha}}\le\frac{10C(L+|j|+1)}{tL^{1+\alpha}}\qquad(j\ge j_0).
\end{equation}

\emph{Tails of $a$.} By~\eqref{eq:Nj}, the $n$ with $u_n\in[j,j+1)$, $j\ge j_0$, contribute at most $10C(2+|j|)\bar g_j$ to $\sum a_n$. The remaining $n\in S$ satisfy $u_n<j_0\le-L/2$, so $n<L/(2t)$ and $a_n\le L^{\alpha}t\,\varrho(L/2)$. They contribute at most $\frac12L^{1+\alpha}\varrho(L/2)\to0$.

\emph{Tails of $b$.} For $j\ge j_0$, since $(\log n)^{1+\alpha}/n\le(\log y)^{1+\alpha}/y$ for $n\ge y$, the $n$ with $u_n\in[j,j+1)$ contribute at most
\[
N_j\,\frac{t(L+\log(L+j))^{1+\alpha}}{L+j}\,\bar g'_j\le\frac{10C(L+j+1)}{L+j}\,\bar g'_j\le20C\,\bar g'_j,\qquad \bar g'_j=\sup_{u\in[j,j+1)}g(\sigma_t(u)).
\]
Since $\log(s+L)\ge0$ for $s\ge j_0$, we have $\sigma_t'(s)\ge L/(s+L)$. For $u\ge0$ this gives $\sigma_t(u)\ge L\log(1+u/L)$, so $\bar g'_j\le2^{-j}$ for $0\le j\le L$ and $\bar g'_j\le2^{-L/2}(1+j/L)^{-L/2}$ for $j>L$. The sum of $20C\,\bar g'_j$ over $j>L$ is therefore $O(2^{-L/2}L)\to0$. For $j_0\le u\le0$ we have $\sigma_t'\ge1$ on $[u,0]$, hence $\sigma_t(u)\le u$ and $\bar g'_j\le\varrho(|j+1|)$ for $j\le-1$. For the $n$ with $u_n<j_0$, which satisfy $n<y_1=L/(2t)$, we have
\[
w(t)-v(n)\ge\tfrac12(\log x_t-\log y_1)\log x_t\ge L/3 .
\]
Their contribution is therefore at most $\varrho(L/3)\sum_{n<y_1}(\log n)^{1+\alpha}/n\le\varrho(L/3)(2L)^{2+\alpha}\to0$.

Consequently there is $\varepsilon(U)\to0$ as $U\to\infty$ such that, for all sufficiently small $t$, the $n\in S$ with $|u_n|\ge U$ contribute at most $\varepsilon(U)$ to $\sum a_n$ and to $\sum b_n$.

\emph{Bulk.} For $|u|\le U$ we have $a_n/b_n=L^{\alpha}g(u)/((\log n)^{\alpha}\sigma_t'(u)g(\sigma_t(u)))$ with $u=u_n$. As $t\to0^+$, uniformly for $|u|\le U$: $L/\log n\to1$, $\sigma_t'(u)\to1$ and $\sigma_t(u)\to u$. Since $g$ is continuous and positive on compact sets, $a_n/b_n\to1$ uniformly. By~\eqref{eq:Nj} the sum $\sum_{|u_n|\le U}a_n$ is bounded, so the bulk contributes $o(1)$ to $\sum(a_n-b_n)$. Hence $\limsup_{t\to0^+}|L^{\alpha}F_S(e^{-t})-I_S(w(t))|\le2\varepsilon(U)$ for every $U$.

label: lem:measureTauber
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:measureTauber}
Let $\mu\ge0$ be a Borel measure on $[0,\infty)$ with $M=\sup_{w\ge0}\mu((w,w+1])+\mu(\{0\})<\infty$, and let $\delta\ge0$. Then $J(w)=\int g(v-w)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(v)\to\delta$ as $w\to\infty$ if and only if $\mu((w,w+c])\to c\delta$ for every $c>0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $w$, the contribution of $|v-w|\ge U$ to $J(w)$ is at most $2M\sum_{|j|\ge U-1}\bar g_j$, which is small for large $U$.

Suppose first that the windows converge. Fix $U$ and $\varepsilon>0$, and choose step functions $s_\pm$ supported in $[-U,U]$ with $s_-\le g\le s_+$ there and $\int(s_+-s_-)<\varepsilon$. For a step function $s$, $\int s(v-w)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(v)$ is a finite combination of window masses, so it tends to $\delta\int s$. Together with the tail bound, this gives $J(w)\to\delta$.

Conversely, suppose $J(w)\to\delta$ and let $0<\eta<1$. Put $\phi(v)=\eta^{-1}\mu((v-\eta,v])$ for $v\in\mathbb{R}$; then $0\le\phi\le M/\eta$. Let $\widetilde\Phi=\phi+\delta\mathbf 1_{(-\infty,0)}$ and $K(z)=g(-z)$. By Fubini,
\[
(K*\widetilde\Phi)(w)=\frac1\eta\int_0^\eta J(w-s)\,\mathrm{d} s+\delta\,\mathcal G(-w).
\]
This tends to $\delta$ as $w\to+\infty$. It also tends to $\delta$ as $w\to-\infty$, because $g(z)\le e^{-z}$ gives $J(w')\le M\sum_{j\ge0}e^{-(j+|w'|)}\to0$ as $w'\to-\infty$. By~\eqref{eq:fourier}, $\widehat K(\xi)=\Gamma(1-i\xi)\ne0$, and $\widehat K(0)=1$. Theorem~\ref{thm:wiener} with $k=\mathbf 1_{[-c,0]}$ gives $\int_w^{w+c}\phi\to c\delta$ for every $c>0$. Moreover
\[
\int_w^{w+c}\phi(v)\,\mathrm{d} v=\int\varpi(y)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y),\qquad \varpi(y)=\eta^{-1}\big|[w,w+c]\cap[y,y+\eta)\big|\in[0,1],
\]
and $\varpi=1$ on $[w,w+c-\eta]$ while $\varpi=0$ outside $(w-\eta,w+c]$. Since $\mu\ge0$,
\[
\int_{w+\eta}^{w+c}\phi\le\mu((w,w+c])\le\int_w^{w+c+\eta}\phi .
\]
Hence all limit points of $\mu((w,w+c])$ lie in $[(c-\eta)\delta,(c+\eta)\delta]$, and $\eta\to0$ completes the proof.
